answer: A Verkle tree replaces hash siblings with vector commitments at each node, so a proof stays small even for a huge set because each level contributes one compact opening. The violet hue of a forged leaf still fails the commitment check at its parent, an orchard of duplicate accounts cannot share one valid path without colliding on the same committed values, and quartz-hard algebra means a farm cannot manufacture a short proof for a leaf that was never committed.
